transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's real nice to meet you, too. Um... I guess what brings me in is, well, there was just a little mix-up at work. I'm a personal care aide, and I always try to do a good job, you know? You know how important safety is for the patients, right? 

Well, we were in a staff meeting, and... I guess I just got a little too worked up. I started acting out this whole fall-prevention drill for everybody. I was really just trying to be helpful, using the chairs and waving my arms around to show them how it happens. But, um... I got kind of carried away, I guess. I couldn't seem to stop doing the drill, even when folks told me to sit down. 

I didn't mean to cause a fuss or make anyone uncomfortable, I promise. I'm just here because I want to make sure I'm doing the right thing, and I'll do whatever you think is best. Does that sound okay?
Over the past week or so, have you been feeling unusually energetic, or have you found that you need much less sleep than you typically do?

Well, um... I guess I have been a little more energetic lately, but it's a good kind of energy, you know? Like, I'm just really motivated to get things done. 

And as for sleep, I've been doing just fine. I mean, maybe I haven't been sleeping as many hours as some folks might, but I don't feel tired at all. Actually, I can sleep just two or three hours, and I'll wake up way before dawn feeling completely rested and ready to go. I'll just be up, making all these plans while the house is still dark and quiet. It's actually a really peaceful time to get a head start on the day. 

I didn't think there was anything wrong with that, since I feel so good and productive. Is it okay to feel like that on just a little bit of sleep?

During those times when you are up early and feeling so energetic, have you noticed any unusual experiences, like hearing voices that others don't hear or feeling like you have special powers or abilities?

Well, um... I guess... I mean, I wouldn't call them special powers or anything like that. I just felt really, really capable, you know? Like I could handle anything that came my way. 

But, um... well, since you asked... I guess during those times when I was all fired up and just sleeping a little bit, making all those big plans in the dark... I did start noticing some things. I probably shouldn't even mention it, because I know how it sounds, but... I'd hear my name being called, or like, short phrases, when there was nobody else in the house. I just tried to ignore it and focus on my plans, I really did. 

And, well, at work... I started getting this feeling. It's probably just me being overly cautious, because safety is so important, right? But I started feeling really sure that my supervisor was... well, setting traps for me. Like leaving things in my way on purpose to see if I'd mess up or get hurt. I know that probably sounds bad, and I didn't want to cause any trouble, I just wanted to do a good job. 

I'm sorry, I hope I'm not saying the wrong things. Is it normal to get a little confused or overly worried when you're that focused and energetic?
Have you experienced these feelings of being watched or heard those voices at times when you weren't feeling so energetic and full of plans?

Well, um... I guess... yeah, I have. I mean, I really don't want you to think I'm making a big deal out of nothing, because I try so hard to just keep my head down and do my work. But... there was a stretch, maybe a few months ago, where things were a lot calmer. I was sleeping my regular hours, and I wasn't rushing around trying to get all those projects done before dawn. 

But, um... even during that quiet time, for a few weeks, I... I still heard it. Just my name being called out when I was alone. And I still couldn't shake the feeling that folks at work were, you know, keeping notes on me or watching me too close. I tried to just smile and be polite to everyone, I really did. I didn't want anyone to think I was being difficult. 

I hope it's okay that I'm telling you this. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers so you can help me be my best at work. Does that make sense?

Could you tell me how long these experiences—like hearing your name or feeling like people were watching you—typically lasted during that period a few months ago when you weren't feeling especially energetic?

Well, um... like I think I just mentioned, it was probably for several weeks. That whole time was a lot calmer, you know? I was sleeping my normal hours again, and I definitely wasn't rushing around with all those extra projects. 

But, um... yeah, for those several weeks during that quiet stretch, I still kept hearing my name. And I just stayed convinced that the other folks at work were keeping notes on me. 

I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the exact timeline you need. Did I answer that right for you? I really did try my best to just push through it and do a good job for my clients, I promise.
